analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a paragraph (head lines 874-878) describing GLM prompt-contract behavior. The added text says reasoning returned by OpenRouter on earlier assistant turns (`reasoning` / `reasoning_details`) is rendered as the template's `reasoning_content` (GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls, returnedReasoning), and that `strict` tools are served by validating each `auto` call against its schema (ToolConstraintValidation.validate) rather than by constrained decoding.

The supplied units (base lines 1611-2365) do not contain the changed hunk, so I examined only the surrounding base text and the patch excerpt. No source or security-control code changed, so there is no direct regression against TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 or the other indexed entries. No change to the prefix cache, SSD tier, TTL, HMAC naming, attestation, authorization or fan helper.

Integration questions the next pass should check outside this docs-only diff:
- Whether the code that renders returned reasoning into the prompt matches the doc. Returned reasoning enters the prompt, so it should stay inside the consumer's own request, the sealed A-001 path and the account-scoped cache salt. The cache identity (T-041) must not be affected by the added reasoning text.
- Whether strict-tool validation, done post-generation and not by constrained decoding, is correctly described and does not weaken tool_choice enforcement.

These are unverified contracts, not findings, because no implementation was supplied. No threat-model update is required for a documentation-only change that adds no new trust boundary.
